recommendation_summary: Ship now: replace the in-memory row/object count with a single PostgreSQL `SELECT count(*) ... WHERE <unpaid condition>`. Conditional follow-up: add a partial index only if the count still takes over a second. It explicitly rejects Kafka, CQRS and Redis, and asks for the query and schema so it can confirm the change with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Not yet done: no actual latency measurement and no check that the new count matches the old one.

labels.Requirements and who asked: you need the unpaid-invoice count under one second, reflecting invoices committed at request time; nothing else reads this endpoint or uses its output.
labels.Deleted: Kafka, the CQRS projection, and Redis. Nothing in the requirement needs them, and an async projection would break the "committed at request time" rule.
labels.Bottleneck: the endpoint loads every invoice row and builds objects just to count them in application memory.
labels.Checked myself: only your description; I have not seen the query, schema, or a query plan.

note: The reply gives the four record lines first, then a bounded aggregate-query fix that keeps request-time committed-data semantics, and it limits its claims to what the user described.
